questions.question: Which normal form requires the elimination of transitive functional dependencies?
questions.explanation: 3NF requires a relation to be in 2NF and have no non-prime attribute transitively dependent on any candidate key.

questions.question: In ACID properties of transactions, what does 'Atomicity' guarantee?
options: All operations within a transaction succeed completely or none take effect
The database remains in a consistent state before and after execution
Concurrent transactions execute without interfering with one another
questions.explanation: Atomicity is the 'all-or-nothing' property ensuring partial transaction executions never persist.

questions.question: Which index structure is most widely utilized in relational databases for range queries?
questions.explanation: B+ trees store all data pointers in leaf nodes linked sequentially, making range scans $O(\log n + k)$.
